options.summary: Set the selected protocol or muxer’s timeout
options.detail: Before the relevant -i or output filename. FTP uses microseconds, libssh uses milliseconds, and RTMP listens in seconds. A DASH or HLS duration uses seconds for a bare number. ftp, libssh (Noble/Resolute) — Set timeout of socket I/O operations. Declared range -1 to INT_MAX. Library default -1. rtmp, rtmps, rtmpt, rtmpts (Noble/Resolute) — Maximum timeout (in seconds) to wait for incoming connections. -1 is infinite. Implies -rtmp_listen 1. Declared range INT_MIN to INT_MAX. Library default -1. rtp (Noble/Resolute) — Set timeout (in microseconds) of socket I/O operations. Declared range -1 to INT64_MAX. Library default -1. sctp (Noble/Resolute) — Connection timeout (in milliseconds). Declared range INT_MIN to INT_MAX. Library default 10000. tcp (Noble/Resolute) — Set timeout (in microseconds) of socket I/O operations. Declared range -1 to INT_MAX. Library default -1. udp, udplite (Noble/Resolute) — Set raise error timeout, in microseconds (only in read mode). Declared range 0 to INT_MAX. Library default 0. unix (Noble/Resolute) — Timeout in ms. Declared range -1 to INT_MAX. Library default -1. libsrt (Noble/Resolute) — Timeout of socket I/O operations (in microseconds). Declared range -1 to INT64_MAX. Library default -1. dash muxer, hls muxer — Set timeout for socket I/O operations. Library default -0.000001. RTSP muxer, RTSP demuxer (Noble/Resolute) — Set timeout (in microseconds) of socket I/O operations. Declared range INT_MIN to INT64_MAX. Library default 0. With the optional 9.1 WHIP muxer, this duration applies to HTTP output socket I/O. The bare unit is seconds. The optional libsmbclient backend in all three tagged releases uses milliseconds for socket I/O.

options.detail: Before a Schannel TLS input or output, specify the certificate subject. The search uses the store selected by -cert_store_name, which defaults to MY. The certificate must have an associated private key. This interface is present in the 8.0.1 and 9.1 Windows sources.

options.summary: Tunnel an encrypted RTMP transport through HTTP
options.detail: The ffrtmpcrypt transport accepts 0 for TCP or 1 for the HTTP tunnel. The RTMPTE protocol selects the tunnel automatically. Use the RTMPTE URL scheme for normal playback. This low-level option requires an encrypted RTMP build, present in the optional 9.1 capture.

options.summary: Use an inherited Windows handle for file I/O
options.detail: FFmpeg 9.1 on Windows accepts a numeric process handle before -i handle: or an output handle: URL. Arrange for the child to inherit the handle. Regular files support seeking. Handles opened with FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED are unsupported. Closing the protocol leaves the original handle open.

options.summary: Select the HTTP version for a libcurl input
options.detail: FFmpeg 9.1 with libcurl accepts auto, 1.0, 1.1, 2, 2tls, 2-prior-knowledge, 3 and 3only. The default is auto. Use a libcurl: URL or -prefer_libcurl 1 before the input. The linked libcurl must support the requested version. In the native HTTP protocol this name only reports the response version through the library API.

options.summary: Accept legacy ICY success responses from streaming servers
options.detail: For an FFmpeg 9.1 libcurl input, use 1 to accept a Shoutcast ICY 200 status line as HTTP success, or 0 to disable this compatibility. The default is 1. This setting controls the status line. -icy controls requests for metadata.

options.summary: Limit initial HTTP range requests during header probing
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 use a positive byte count before a native HTTP or libcurl input. The restriction ends when the demuxer requests a larger read without an intervening seek. Use -short_seek_size of at least the same size to avoid reconnecting for small advances. The default 0 disables the initial limit.

options.summary: Choose which address families an SRT wildcard listener accepts
options.detail: FFmpeg 9.1 with libsrt 1.4.0 or later requires an explicit value when an SRT listener binds the IPv6 wildcard address. Use 1 for IPv6 only or 0 to allow IPv4 as well. The default -1 leaves the choice unspecified. The setting applies to the listening socket.

options.summary: Supply the password for an encrypted TLS private key
options.detail: Place the password before the TLS input or output using the mbedTLS backend. Its key parser uses this value to unlock the file supplied with -key_file. The three tagged releases include this backend option. The reviewed Ubuntu builds use GnuTLS.

options.summary: Set the local RTCP port
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 this aliases -local_rtcpport before the RTP input or output. Supply a UDP port number. If a local RTP port is specified, the default local RTCP port is that port plus one. On Noble and Resolute use -local_rtcpport on the command line or localrtcpport=PORT in the RTP URL query.

options.summary: Set the local RTP port
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 this aliases -local_rtpport before the RTP input or output. Supply a UDP port number. Without a local port the transport chooses an available port. On Noble and Resolute use -local_rtpport on the command line or localrtpport=PORT in the RTP URL query.

options.summary: Limit HTTP redirects followed for an input
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 place a nonnegative count before the HTTP input. Native HTTP defaults to 8 redirects. The optional libcurl backend defaults to 16. Use 0 to disallow redirects.

options.summary: Limit libcurl retries after a recoverable transfer error
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 place a nonnegative count before a seekable libcurl input. The default is 5 retries. Select libcurl with a libcurl: URL or -prefer_libcurl 1. An in-band ICY metadata stream cannot resume from a payload offset.

options.summary: Limit the size of each HTTP range request
options.detail: Before a seekable HTTP input in FFmpeg 9.1, give the maximum bytes per range request. The default 0 leaves the request size unlimited. Native HTTP and the optional libcurl backend support this setting. In-band ICY metadata streams cannot use libcurl range requests.

options.summary: Set the remote RTCP destination port
options.detail: In FFmpeg 9.1 this aliases -rtcp_port before the RTP input or output. Supply a UDP port number. The default remote RTCP port is the destination RTP port plus one. On Noble and Resolute use -rtcp_port on the command line or rtcpport=PORT in the RTP URL query.

options.summary: Set the socket send buffer for librtmp output
options.detail: All three tagged releases support this setting when built with the optional librtmp backend. Supply a byte count before the output URL. The default -1 leaves the socket buffer unchanged. The separately named -rtmp_buffer option measures client buffer time in milliseconds.

options.summary: Enable TCP keepalive for a long-lived connection
options.detail: FFmpeg 9.1 TCP accepts 1 before the input or output URL to enable the operating system’s keepalive probes. The default is 0. Probe timing follows the operating system configuration.

options.summary: Negotiate SRTP keys in a DTLS handshake
options.detail: Before the DTLS input or output URL in an FFmpeg 9.1 build with DTLS-SRTP support, use 1 to offer the use_srtp extension. The default is 0. WebRTC uses this extension to establish SRTP keys.

options.summary: Verify the identity of the remote peer
options.detail: In TLS and DTLS builds of FFmpeg 9.1 this aliases -tls_verify. The 9.1 libssh backend uses the same spelling for the SSH server host key and requires a matching known_hosts entry. Both default to enabled. Place the option before the corresponding input or output URL. For command-line TLS verification on Noble and Resolute, use -tls_verify 1.

options.summary: Select the SMB workgroup for a connection
options.detail: Place the workgroup name before an SMB input or output on a build with libsmbclient. All three tagged releases declare this option. The reviewed Ubuntu packages omit this protocol. Without a workgroup override libsmbclient uses its configured workgroup.
